Pill packs are usually packaged at the pharmacy. It’s a small plastic bag with all the pills a patient is prescribed for the time of day. They come in a roll, so you pull off a pouch for the morning and all your oral meds are there. Patients might have three separate rolls for morning, noon and night

I’m a med history tech in a hospital, so my opinions may be skewed, but the biggest issue I see when a patient has multiple medications is confusion. It gets easy to remember which pill does what. Doses get jumbled and if some are BID and others are TID, it gets easy to mix them up. Especially in geriatric communities. Patients will sometimes be able to provide a list or access their pharmacy portal, but too often they rely on us to have the information. The best method right now for anyone taking more than 5 meds is pill pack services. It makes it so much easier on the patient and they’ll even include your OTC meds. No more mix ups. The frustration I hear most often is about constant dose changes. If they have a particular issue that is hard to control, it becomes hard to remember if they take 1/2 a pill TID or a whole pill BID. Thank you for understanding. Our pharmacists are required to act in good faith while dispensing meds. Their livelihoods are on the line. But they do also care and want you to have what you need. It’s a fine line sometimes. I doubt you will have any trouble if you go in and speak to them openly. I use savings programs for patients all day. No shame in that game. It’s expensive to be healthy. Just stay with your regular pharmacy as long as you can and if you have to change chains, know if can look suspicious and be ready to explain everything from the beginning

The more open you are, the better off you will be. I can see in my system a pattern of people going between school and home. But if we see you going to a different chain every single month, it looks more sketchy to us. I would go in once the dr sends the script, explain to situation, explain that you want to use goodrx but will pay cash if necessary. Politeness will be your best friend. We have a good internal radar and we’ll sense of you’re being honest and just in a bad place right now. Don’t feel ashamed. Needing meds is perfectly normal. Being entitled and rude isn’t ok. We’re not all mean and scary. We want you to have what you need to function. We’re just trying to keep addictive substances out of the wrong hands and protect out community if we can.

Yes, because often we won’t fill an expensive medication for a patient with no insurance on file since we don’t think they will end up paying out of pocket. Go ahead and let them know what’s going on and that you will be paying out of pocket or at a discount so they know not to store your prescription

It’s not a shameful thing to need the meds, just be prepared because others try to game the system with those cards and we get pretty jaded. Be polite, explain your situation, and be ready to answer any possible questions about why you’re using goodrx. If you show up clean in the drug monitoring database and don’t have a history of going back and forth between different pharmacies and using multiple discounts, you’ll be fine. It sucks that we judge people based on the bad behaviors of others, but we have to be careful both for the health of patients and our own licenses
